linkedin.hook: Formal verification changes how we model composable leverage on Stellar.
linkedin.copy:
Most cross-protocol leverage designs on newer chains inherit structural weakness from unverified lending wrappers. When underlying pools drift or recalculate shares with rounding errors, secondary protocols carry bad debt. Blend v2 eliminated that failure vector by formally verifying their core pool contracts and b-token exchange rates. This turns yield-bearing b-tokens into deterministic base assets rather than opaque yield aggregators.

Vanna builds directly on this foundation by isolating risk at the account level. Instead of pooling collateral and socializing liquidator execution delay, we deploy independent SmartAccount contracts per position. Our liquidation pipeline tracks on-chain states via Mercury indexers at ~320ms latency, operating cleanly above our fixed 1.10x Health Factor floor. Predictable execution costs of 0.00014 XLM per invocation make atomic leverage rebalancing practical at scale.

The end result is a composable credit layer where lending risk does not spill across isolated margin accounts. You can inspect the contracts and deploy your testnet SmartAccount sandbox at test.stellar.vanna.finance.

Institutional architecture is documented at test.stellar.vanna.finance

reddit.hook: Deep dive into Blend v2 b-token verification and how Vanna uses it for composable margin on Soroban
reddit.copy:
Blend v2 landed formal verification on their lending logic, which solves an annoying architectural problem we have been dealing with in Soroban DeFi: trustless collateral valuation without custom wrapper contracts.

For context, b-tokens track lender claims and accrue yield directly inside Blend pool states. If you want to build automated leverage, you usually have to write intermediate vault contracts that burn extra gas, create share-rounding attack surfaces, and introduce liquidation lag.

Vanna bypasses that layer entirely by deploying isolated SmartAccount sandboxes that interact directly with Blend v2 pools.

First, account segregation handles the execution overhead. Each position runs inside an independent smart contract rather than a pooled bucket. When a strategy executes, borrowed capital and b-tokens settle in a single transaction with an invocation cost of 0.00014 XLM.

Second, liquidations rely on tight indexer sync rather than wide safety buffers. We stream ledger updates through Mercury indexers running at ~320ms latency. Because the indexer keeps up with ledger close times, the protocol enforces a strict 1.10x Health Factor floor without needing excessive margin cushions.

Third, risk stays confined to individual smart accounts. If an underlying pool asset undergoes extreme volatility, bad debt cannot bleed into other positions.

Deploy your testnet SmartAccount sandbox at test.stellar.vanna.finance to run your own transactions.

Disclosure: I am a core engineer at Vanna working on our Soroban credit contracts.
